newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A surprise prime rate cut by Standard Bank provided a late incentive for the bond market to extend its gains on Wednesday, helping yields to their best levels in nearly eight weeks.
At the finish, the benchmark R150 was pegged at a 15.09 percent yield -- its best level since July 12 when it closed at 15.10 -- and over 10 basis points off its overnight 15.23 percent finish.
Dealers said that while the rate cut had taken the market by surprise, the fact that the rationale for the easing was a technical reason was unlikely to fuel more gains on the market.
Standard Bank said it had reduced its prime rate to 19.25 percent from 19.50 percent with effect from October 1 as a result of the removal of the Financial Services Levy.

"The rate cut might help the underlying strength in the market, but the interesting thing will be what the other banks do," a dealer said, adding that other banks might see fit to reduce their prime rates by more than 25 basis points, triggering a rate war.
Dealers said Standard Bank's late announceent helped the market build on gains which were fuelled in the morning session by aggressive buying a U.S. investment bank trading out London.
"We saw some aggressive buying this morning...it was also helped lower by other offshore guys who were caught short overnight covering their positions," one trader said.

Sentiment was also upbeat on the fact that two offshore loans had been signed earlier this week which would help ease the continuing liquidity squeeze in the money market and help short-term rates lower, dealers said.

Telecommunications utility Telkom announced earlier this week that it had signed a $170 million loan, while Amalgamated Banks of Southern Africa announced on Tuesday that it had signed a $200 million syndicated loan.
A delegation of South African finance department officials are also currently touring Europe ahead of the launch of a Euromark issue, the terms of which are expected to be decided by Friday.
On the currency market, the rand also snapped out of its recent lethargy to strengthen another cent against the dollar.
It was last quoted at 4.4785/4735 on the U.S. unit from 4.4900/4950 late on Tuesday.
Dealers said the currency was helped on the day by "export-oriented" dollar selling and a dearth of importer demand, although dollar buying out of London stemmed any substantial gains.
They said that having traded below the 4.50 mark since Monday, the currency now looked set to test the 4.47 level, a breach of which could bring the 4.45 level into its target range.

Against the crosses, the currency was last pegged at 6.9645/9759 against sterling from 6.9878/7.0001 on Tuesday and was at a seven week high of 0.3364/3369 marks from 0.3352/3357 previously, helped by the stronger dollar and a lack of importer demand.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were a touch higher at between 15.95 and 16.10 percent from 15.90 and 16.10 percent on Tuesday, while 90-day BAs were steady at between 15.35 to 15.50 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the daily shortage eased to 8.776 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.123 billion rand on Monday.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 24.05 million rand worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling 73.64 million rand on Monday. Nominal cumulative volumes jumped to 5.19 billion rand on Tuesday from 2.24 billion rand on Monday.
